title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design notes, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and the most recent release notes for the Unified Inference initiative (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private). It is intended as the single living reference for product managers, engineering leads, go-to-market, and customer-facing teams.

Goals:
- Deliver a unified API and developer experience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Provide clear levers to optimize cost, latency, and reliability for production workloads.
- Make model routing, quantization profiles, and caching first-class controls in the product.
- Enable enterprise customers with predictable SLAs and deployment options.

Summary of scope (what's in / out):
- In scope: API contract for text generation/chat/embeddings, model routing and fallback policies, quantization profile support, batching/caching controls, rollout and canary tooling, cost observability.
- Out of scope: Training pipelines, model development interfaces, marketplace model procurement (these remain in Research/Applied ML).

1) Product Requirements (PRD) - high level

Problem statement:
Customers running inference at scale face unpredictable cost and latency when model selection, routing, and serving topology are uncontrolled. Teams want the same API and predictable operational tooling whether they use Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments.

Primary user journeys:
1. Developer evaluates models via the hosted API and pins a model version for production.
2. Platform team configures Dedicated capacity and uses rollout tools to migrate traffic.
3. Enterprise ops deploys Private with KMS integration and applies routing/fallback policies.

Core requirements (MUST):
- R1: Unified API surface that supports generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, and structured outputs with identical request/response schemas across deployment modes.
- R2: Model routing policy engine: rule-based and ML-backed routing with fallbacks by latency/cost/region.
- R3: Cost & latency observability: token-level cost, per-route and per-model latency distribution, and alerts for regressions.
- R4: Rollout primitives: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback with traffic weighting and health checks.
- R5: Dedicated capacity reservation and burst options with SLAs (99.9% uptime target for Dedicated).
- R6: Quantization profile framework: apply and recommend quantization profiles per model/workload with used metrics (accuracy/latency/cost).
- R7: KV prefix caching and auto-batching controls that can be tuned per route.
- R8: Security/compliance: audit logging for customer operations, KMS/HSM integration for Private, role-based access to rollout controls.

Secondary requirements (SHOULD):
- S1: Automated recommendations in Redwood Optimize for batching and quantization.
- S2: Built-in prompt/eval integration for regression detection tied to rollouts.
- S3: SDK parity across languages for rollout and routing config APIs.

Non-goals:
- NG1: Replacing customer model versioning systems; we integrate with model registries but do not own model training artifacts.
- NG2: Fully managed dataset storage for private training.

Success metrics (examples):
- Adoption: % of paid customers using at least one Dedicated or Private deployment option within 12 months of GA.
- Economics: Average token cost reduction of 20% for customers using quantization + caching compared to baseline.
- Reliability: Dedicated SLO of 99.9% availability (measured monthly).
- Quality: <2% regression rate detected by evals tied to rollouts.

Owners and stakeholders:
- PM: Aisha Patel (product lead, Unified Inference)
- Eng leads: Marco Chen (platform/runtime), Priya Rao (serving runtime)
- Research/Applied ML: Elena Garcia (model onboarding/quantization)
- GTM: Jonas Meyer (sales), Sara Kim (customer success)

2) Design Specs & Architecture notes (high level)

Design principles:
- One API, many runtimes: keep surface stable while routing to different runtime backends.
- Observability-first: every routing decision and model variant must emit telemetry and be queryable.
- Progressive rollout: support incremental traffic migration and automated rollback.

High-level components:
- Control plane: routing policy engine, rollout manager, tenant config store, billing hooks.
- Serving runtime: GPU-optimized inference engine with kernel selection, KV cache, and batching.
- Observability pipeline: token-level metrics, traces per request, model-level quality metrics.
- Optimize agent: offline/online recommendations for batching/quantization.

API contract changes (summary):
- New field: route_policy (string | object) - name of the routing policy applied to request.
- New header: X-Redwood-Trace-Config - to control tracing for debug canaries.
- Stable schema: response envelope contains model.metadata.version and model.metadata.quantization_profile.

Configuration table (example):
- config_key: route.policy | type: string | description: Identifier for routing policy | default: "default" | owner: product/platform
- config_key: quant.profile | type: string | description: Quantization profile id to apply at serving time | default: "fp16" | owner: research
- config_key: cache.prefix_ttl | type: integer | description: seconds to keep prefix cache entries | default: 300 | owner: runtime

Design tradeoffs noted:
- Placing policy evaluation in control plane reduces latency variability but increases control plane load - mitigated via local policy caches in edge runtime.
- Aggressive caching reduces cost but can increase staleness for conversation state; default TTLs and route-level opt-outs are provided.

3) Roadmap & Themes (next 12 months)

Themes by quarter (high level):
- Q4 2025: Unified API stabilization, early beta for Dedicated, basic rollout primitives.
- Q1 2026: Quantization profiles v1, caching & batching controls, Redwood Optimize recommendations v1.
- Q2 2026: Private deployment GA (VPC), KMS integration, advanced routing ML-backed policies.
- Q3 2026: Cost-aware autoscaling and burst policies, extended SDKs, long-term retention observability tier.

Milestones and dates (tentative):
- 2025-12-15: Unified API v1 GA (hosted)
- 2026-02-28: Dedicated beta with reservation model and SLA preview
- 2026-04-30: Quantization profiles v1 GA (recommendations in Optimize)
- 2026-06-30: Private deployment beta (VPC + basic KMS)

Dependencies and risks:
- Risk: Kernel and runtime regression when enabling new quantization profiles. Mitigation: canary evaluation harness and model-level baseline tests in applied-ml-and-evals.
- Dependency: Cloud provider GPU availability for Dedicated region launches.

4) Pricing & Packaging notes

Pricing principles:
- Usage-based pricing for Hosted (tokens/embedding units).
- Reservation + overage model for Dedicated (monthly commit + burst pricing).
- Private: platform license + capacity fee + optional support tiers.

Recommended packaging tiers (example):
- Developer (Hosted only): pay-as-you-go tokens, limited retention, community support.
- Growth (Hosted + Dedicated credits): discounted token pricing after monthly commit, access to Optimize recommendations.
- Enterprise (Dedicated + Private): committed capacity, SLA 99.9% (Dedicated), compliance add-ons, premium support.

Pricing knobs and examples:
- Token price varies by model family and quantization profile. Example: base model gptx-3 fp16 $0.0006 / 1k tokens; int8 quantized variant $0.00042 / 1k tokens (30% reduction).
- Dedicated reservations: $X per GPU-month (tiered) + $Y per GPU-hour for bursts. (Sales to provide region-specific numbers.)
- Private licensing: Platform fee (annual) + per-GPU capacity fee.

Guidance for sales enablement:
- Example ROI calc: For a customer processing 500M tokens/month, switching to quantized model + prefix caching can reduce monthly inference bill by ~25% (include sample calc sheet link).
- Typical traction criteria to escalate to Enterprise sales: > $5k monthly spend or security/compliance needs requiring Private.

5) Release notes (latest release: 2026-02-25)

Release summary:
- Version: unified-inference-2026-02-25
- Release date: 2026-02-25
- Release owner: Aisha Patel

Key features:
- GA: Unified API v1 (generation, chat, embeddings) with stable schema across hosts and Dedicated runtimes.
- Beta: Dedicated reservation model with SLA preview and per-route capacity controls.
- Feature: Quantization profiles v1 (experimental) available in Hosted beta with recommendation hooks in Redwood Optimize.
- Observability: Token-level cost breakdown and per-model latency histogram in Console.

Fixes & improvements:
- Improved KV cache TTL heuristics to reduce latency spikes by 12% (measured on internal benchmark).
- Rollout manager: added health-check based auto-rollback for canaries.
- API: added model.metadata.quantization_profile in response envelope.

Known issues and mitigations:
- Q1: Some models when served with int8 profiles exhibit small accuracy regressions on long-context tasks. Mitigation: default to fp16 for routes with QA workloads until model-specific evals pass.
- Q2: Private installer edge-case on RHEL 8 kernel versions - documented workaround in eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging.

Rollout notes & customer communication:
- Customers on beta will receive an email with migration steps, brief migration checklist and options to pin previous model variants.
- Provide a one-click rollback in Console for canary failures during the first 72 hours after traffic migration.

Action items (next 30 days):
1. Product: finalize pricing examples and publish sales calc sheet (owner: Jonas Meyer).
2. Engineering: complete Dedicated SLA documentation and run game-day for failover (owner: Marco Chen).
3. Research: complete quantization regression triage for top-10 onboarding models (owner: Elena Garcia).
4. DevRel: update quickstarts and SDK docs to show route_policy examples (owner: DevRel team).

References and links:
- See: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage for model evaluation playbook.
- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging for Private installer docs.
- See: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture for runtime internals and kernel notes.

Appendix: Example API request (simplified)
POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer <key>
  X-Redwood-Trace-Config: sample
Body (JSON):
{
  "model": "gptx-3",
  "prompt": "Summarize the following...",
  "route_policy": "latency-first",
  "temperature": 0.2
}

Response (partial):
{
  "id": "req-12345",
  "model": "gptx-3",
  "model.metadata.version": "2026-02-10",
  "model.metadata.quantization_profile": "int8-v1",
  "text": "..."
}
